holidays.name: Smoke and Mirrors Day
holidays.description: A day for celebrating illusion, misdirection and things that aren't quite what they seem. Think magic tricks, clever marketing and optical illusions. Take a second look at everything today, because it might not be real.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It plays on the old phrase for deceiving or distracting people, and it has become a favorite among magic and illusion fans.
holidays.funFact: The phrase 'smoke and mirrors' comes from stage illusions. Early magicians reportedly used smoke and mirrors to make ghostly apparitions seem to appear.

holidays.name: National Lemon Chiffon Cake Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate a light, airy, citrusy cake. It is fluffy like an angel food cake but richer, and it is often topped with a tangy lemon glaze. Bake one, or just treat yourself to a slice.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance. The cake itself was created by Harry Baker, a Los Angeles insurance agent turned caterer, who kept the recipe secret for about 20 years before selling it to General Mills in 1948.
holidays.funFact: Chiffon cake gets its lift from vegetable oil and whipped egg whites, which makes it a rare 'oil-based' cake that stays soft and moist.

holidays.name: Mermaid Day
holidays.description: A day for fans of fins and seashell fashion. Celebrate the legendary half-human, half-fish creatures of folklore with ocean-themed costumes, stories and glittery everything.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It's popular with fans of mythology and ocean lore.
holidays.funFact: Mermaid legends go back thousands of years. One of the oldest known tales is the Assyrian goddess Atargatis, who was said to have jumped into a lake and become part fish.
